figures.caption: **Figure 1. The range of energy, from radio to X-rays.** Energy rises from left to right. Wi-Fi sits in the microwave band. The dividing line falls in the ultraviolet, and too much of that burns skin. Not to scale.
figures.alt: Figure 1. The range of energy, from radio to X-rays. Energy rises from left to right. Wi-Fi sits in the microwave band. The dividing line falls in the ultraviolet, and too much of that burns skin. Not to scale.

figures.caption: **Figure 2. The same four powers, drawn two ways.** (a) On an ordinary ruler the oven fills the width. The router, phone and Wi-Fi cap are too thin to see. (b) Each step to the right is ten times the one before. On this scale the oven looks close. On a ruler it's thousands of times the router. Every bar ends at its value.

figures.caption: **Figure 3. Thousands of times the power, kept in a box.** Left, the oven's energy bounces around inside its metal box. Right, a router's tenth of a watt spreads out into the room. Not to scale.
figures.alt: Figure 3. Thousands of times the power, kept in a box. Left, the oven's energy bounces around inside its metal box. Right, a router's tenth of a watt spreads out into the room. Not to scale.

figures.caption: **Figure 4. The same power, spread over more area.** Twice as far away, the power covers four squares. So each square gets a quarter. Not to scale.
figures.alt: Figure 4. The same power, spread over more area. Twice as far away, the power covers four squares. So each square gets a quarter. Not to scale.

figures.caption: **Figure 5. Walls soak up signal too.** Top, open air. Bottom, the same distance through a wall: less reaches the far side. Not to scale.
figures.alt: Figure 5. Walls soak up signal too. Top, open air. Bottom, the same distance through a wall: less reaches the far side. Not to scale.

figures.caption: **Figure 6. How much of the public limit a router reaches.** A router sending nonstop, with no walls in the way. Distances to scale.
figures.alt: Figure 6. How much of the public limit a router reaches. A router sending nonstop, with no walls in the way. Distances to scale.

figures.caption: **Figure 7. A real router sends in short bursts.** Top, the math on this page. Bottom, a real router, sending only when there's data to move. Not to scale.
figures.alt: Figure 7. A real router sends in short bursts. Top, the math on this page. Bottom, a real router, sending only when there's data to move. Not to scale.

figures.caption: **Figure 8. The safety margin.** The public limit is a fiftieth of the level that warms the body. Each bar is drawn to scale.
figures.alt: Figure 8. The safety margin. The public limit is a fiftieth of the level that warms the body. Each bar is drawn to scale.

figures.caption: **Figure 9. Figured and measured, against the public limit.** (a) On an ordinary ruler, only the limit shows. (b) Each step to the right is ten times the one before. Classroom values are rounded, so they are shown as "about."
